product: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model, 60 arc-second surface elevation (ice surface), NOAA NCEI
licence_credit: US Government work, no restrictions. Credit: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (2022) ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74
native_resolution: 60 arc-second (1.853 km N-S; 1.853*cos(lat) km E-W); heights in m above the EGM2008 geoid
aggregation_to_cell: over all land-land pairs in the cell: south-neighbour pairs (exactly one pixel = 1.853 km apart) and east pairs taken at the SAME metric lag, i.e. 1/cos(lat) pixels along the row (linear interpolation between the two bracketing pixels, both must be land); pooled
formula: sqrt(mean((z(x+L) - z(x))^2)), L = 1.853 km in both directions = deviogram (Rosenburg et al. 2011) at a lag of one DEM pixel; identical definition to the Moon table (lag 1.895 km)
caveats: BASELINE: isotropic lag 1.853 km (one ETOPO pixel N-S); not 300 m, so values are larger than a 300 m roughness. Fixed during verification: the first build used a 1-pixel east lag (1.853*cos(lat) km), which made roughness too low away from the equator (new/old median ratio 1.075 at 30-60 deg, 1.26 at 60-75 deg, 1.44 poleward of 75 deg) and differed from the Moon definition
